lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: An original solid has $3$ unequal arms meeting at a joint: a long arm, a medium arm, and a short arm. Candidate A and Candidate B show $2$ possible turned views. Which candidate can show the same solid after rotation?
lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.note: Checked that Example #1 now gives the missing paired-view mental-rotation comparison and works it through to Candidate A.

lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: To compare $2$ views, track a few clear parts together:
lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.note: Checked the new four-step comparison method and the worked rotation example; the lesson now teaches how to trace a concrete pair of views.

lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: **Mental rotation** asks whether $2$ views can show the same solid object after you turn it without flipping it. A turn keeps the same parts touching and keeps the same shape and distances.
lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.note: Checked that the dense invariants sentence is replaced by shorter, simpler wording and that the hard chirality wording is gone.

lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: **Handedness** means the object's left-hand or right-hand arrangement. Your left and right hands are mirror forms. You can turn your left hand, but turning alone does not make it become your right hand.
lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.note: Checked that handedness now has a simple meaning before it is used as a rotation test.

lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: Candidate A keeps the same order of the arms around the joint. Turning the whole object can make that view.
lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.note: Checked the optional concern: the lesson now develops rotation comparison in Core Concept and demonstrates it in a worked paired-view example.

lesson-spatial-abstract-reasoning-mental.quote: Marks painted on a solid do not change its outline. A hole changes the shadow only when light can pass through it in the shown direction.
